summary: Stage optional native fencing packages, including qnetd on Core and Controller images, with maintainer-start and first-boot guards

guide.reason: The packages are installed as inactive prerequisites only; no operator-facing fencing configuration or behavior is implemented in this slice.

api.reason: This only changes the ISO's package contents and install-time service policy. No Core operation, Controller request, or API contract is added.

roadmap.reason: Storage lease and witness remain unimplemented slices; staging these optional packages does not claim their acceptance gates are complete.

state.reason: This adds no runtime fencing state or configuration; packages are staged only and their services remain disabled until a later Core implementation configures them.

verification.method: The new failed-APT regression first reproduced exit 126 from direct invocation of the non-executable helper, then passed after internal calls used sh. `python3 -m unittest tests.test_storage_packaging tests.test_build_source tests.test_appliance_build` passes; the repository privacy test, `bash installer/check.sh`, shell syntax checks, `git diff --check`, and `python3 scripts/check_docs.py --worktree` passed. Temporary-root tests exercise policy delegation/restoration and isolated systemd/SysV disable checks. Debian Trixie package records, copyright files and maintainer-script actions were inspected; a separate native qnetd spike confirmed the default durable CA location and runtime replacement behavior. New-image scripts remove the package-created default CA. No live hosts, actual dpkg package install, ISO build, or appliance image build was used; package postinst execution and first boot remain unverified.
